questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to travel to Australia. This was an amazing opportunity to combine my studies with traveling.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was easy. I was well informed about where to meet on my first day at the hospital and I was taken good care of.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a contact person assigned to me from the UTAS.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: As the semester had already started I was not introduced to other exchange students at the university properly. I was also staying at the hospital and did not receive classes on campus which made it even harder. I did make some nice friends during my stay but it would have been easier and I would have made more friends earlier, if I would have had a proper introduction in the beginning of mob stay.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy. I looked it up online. Hytten Hall. I sent them an email a couple months before. It was a student housing building 5 min walk from the hospital.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was completely fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The application process was long, but worth it!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Consisted of several documents, insurance, vaccination forms, visa application and approved documents by the embassy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None from KU. My contact person in Tasmania helped me. Other than that I seeked help in previous students who went on exchange in Tasmania.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful. I received the 3 months that I wanted and the departments that I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a long process, but it is worth it. Talk to past exchange students about their experiences

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical rotation in a foreign country

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Emergency medicine, you will have a lot of hand on experience and see many patients on your own.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The application process was expensive. I had to have many documents approved by a notarian at the Australian embassy in Cph as well as various medical certificates prior to departure.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were som events hosted by the student association at UTAS. They were cheap! I can recommend.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many outdoor tours! At Hytten Hall where I stayed the also hosted a free student dinner every other week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: GO hiking. Go camping, Enjoy the nature and wildlife that Tassie has to offer. Markets on the weekends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: GO hiking. Go camping, Enjoy the nature and wildlife that Tassie has to offer. Markets on the weekends. Rent a car!!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. People speak English, very close to danish/western culture. Australians are very open minded.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to UTAS medical students maybe they have som good tips on what to do in Tasmania or they want to go on a hike with you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Open minded, laid back, friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the nature and wild life, go with the flow, keep an open mind.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rent a car if you want to see some more of Tasmania's beauty.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I am very grateful for meeting all the nice people during my stay. Being on my own and doing things on my own like hiking a mountain on my own. Experiencing such beautiful exotic nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference. I was hard to keep in contact with my friends and family back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it! You will not regret it :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
